$comment: Ramps are generated from a hue and a chroma ceiling rather than hand-picked, so that
changing the brand is one number and every step stays on the same hue with the same
measured contrast. Hand-picked hex ramps drift in hue as they darken and have to be
re-verified by eye after any change.
Lightness targets are OKLCH L, which is perceptually even: stepping L by a constant
amount looks like a constant step, which is what a ramp is for.

brand.$status: PLACEHOLDER - awaiting DTHC brand identity from Dr. Nahid
brand.$howToChange: Change hue, and chroma if needed. Nothing else. The tests re-verify contrast.
brand.$why: A medical teal: read as clinical and calm, distinct from every clinical status hue below, and far enough from red and green that it is never mistaken for a result.

neutral.$why: A very slightly cool grey. Pure grey on an LCD reads faintly warm next to a teal brand; a trace of blue keeps surfaces looking neutral rather than beige.

$comment: Hues chosen for maximum separation in the dimension colour-blind vision preserves:
lightness. Under deuteranopia the red-to-green arc collapses, so normal, high and
critical converge in hue - they are separated here by lightness as well, and by an
icon and a label in the components. See vision.ts.
low is blue rather than a second green: blue survives red-green deficiency intact,
and 'low' is the status most often confused with 'normal' when reading quickly.

ramp.$comment: OKLCH lightness per step, and the fraction of the hue's chroma ceiling to apply. Chroma peaks mid-ramp: near-white and near-black cannot hold saturation without turning muddy.

absolute.$comment: The two colours that are not ramp steps. Named so that 'white' in a token file is unambiguous about which white.
